title: Keep the journey view generated from plan/ and current

facts.note: Scope gate 1 is a repository-state check: the docs/ directory exists (filesystem existence check, not merely a changed path matching docs/**).
Scope gate 2 requires parsing plan/ for actual journey/interlocking declarations; a plan/** path glob alone cannot establish it.
The generated journey view (index.adoc and SVGs).

values: docs_capability: journey view missing, stale, hand-edited or extra file
facts.note: State-based invariant: validator compares committed files with a fresh render of the current plan/ by the installed package; fires on any mismatch whether or not the current change touched plan/ or docs/ (pre-existing drift, renderer/package upgrade).

values: plan journey/interlocking/route/train added, modified or removed
file under docs/purpose/journeys/ edited, added or removed
facts.note: Diff-level hints that a mismatch is likely; not required for the rule to fire.

fires: In a repository with docs/ whose plan declares journeys or interlockings, a planner adds, renames or rewires a journey, interlocking, route or train in plan/ and does not regenerate docs/purpose/journeys/.
In a repository with docs/ whose plan declares journeys or interlockings, someone edits an SVG or index.adoc under docs/purpose/journeys/ by hand.
In a repository with docs/ whose plan declares interlockings but no journey, no journey page is committed.
In a repository with docs/ whose plan declares journeys or interlockings, docs/purpose/journeys/ contains a file the generator would not produce (e.g. an SVG for a removed train).

In a repository with docs/ whose plan declares journeys or interlockings, the committed view was already stale or missing before the current task, even though the task touched neither plan/ nor docs/.
In a repository with docs/ whose plan declares journeys or interlockings, an upgrade of the installed package changes the renderer output and the committed view is not regenerated.
doesNotFire: The repository has no docs/ directory.
The plan declares no journey and no interlocking.
A plan edit leaves the rendered output byte-identical AND the committed view already matched the generator output (an unchanged render never excuses existing missing, stale or extra files).

given: The repository has a docs/ directory and its plan/ declares at least one journey or interlocking.
when: You finish any plan work or review in that repository, whether or not you touched plan/ or docs/; pre-existing drift and renderer upgrades count.
then: docs/purpose/journeys/ must contain exactly, byte-for-byte, what `atdd-bun docs journeys` generates from the current plan/: index.adoc plus one SVG per journey map, per journey's nominal path, and per routed train.
prefer: Regenerate and commit: `bun run atdd-bun docs journeys`.
Fix what the view shows in the plan, then regenerate.
If index.adoc there is hand-written, move its content elsewhere first (the generator refuses to overwrite it without --force).
Keep the gaps table (unreached interlockings, open routes, unrouted trains) visible and accurately rendered; it is part of the contract.
avoid: Hand-editing or adding files under docs/purpose/journeys/; change the plan, never the generated files.
Leaving the view missing or stale, or keeping files the generator does not produce.
Skipping the page when the plan has interlockings but no journey; it shows every interlocking as unreached.
Treating the view as acceptance evidence; it renders planned behaviour only.
unless: The repository has no docs/ directory.
The plan declares no journey and no interlocking.
why: A hand-drawn journey page drifts from the plan the moment either changes; generating it and failing on any difference keeps documented journeys equal to planned ones and lets reviewers judge a decomposition without reading interlocking YAML.
evidence: Running `bun run atdd-bun docs journeys` against the current plan/ produces no diff in docs/purpose/journeys/ (no missing, changed or extra files).

The committed index.adoc shows, top down: each journey map (entry action, interlockings, chosen routes, trains run, continuations and terminal outcomes); each journey's nominal path end to end as one sequence across its interlockings; every path as a table; each interlocking's routes with their guards; each train as a sequence diagram; and a table of what the plan leaves unconnected.
For a plan with interlockings but no journey, the page exists and lists every interlocking as unreached, which is the truthful state of the decomposition.
The view answers who hands what to whom, which guard selects which route, and where each path ends.
verifier_detail: Comparison is byte-for-byte between committed files under docs/purpose/journeys/ and what the installed package renders from the current plan/.
Expected file set: index.adoc plus one SVG per journey map, per journey's nominal path, and per routed train. Missing, stale, hand-edited or extra files are each violations.
Rendered output carries no timestamp and no package version, so it changes only when the plan or the renderer changes; no normalisation of such fields is needed.

Term journey_view: the generated page, top down: each journey as a map (entry action, interlockings, the routes they choose, the trains they run, continuations and terminal outcomes); the journey's nominal path walked end to end as one sequence across its interlockings; every path as a table; each interlocking's routes with their guards; each train as a sequence diagram; and a table of what the plan leaves unconnected.
Term generated: byte-for-byte what the installed package renders from the current plan/.

Scope gate: skip when no docs/ directory exists, or when the plan declares no journey and no interlocking. A plan with interlockings but no journey is in scope. Within scope the check is state-based: any mismatch is a finding regardless of what the current diff touched.
Generator refuses to overwrite a hand-written docs/purpose/journeys/index.adoc unless run with --force.
audit: source name: The journey documentation is generated from plan/ and matches it

additions.justification: Illustrates the source's 'extra file is a violation' clause; adds no obligation.

additions.text: Explicit statement that pre-existing drift and renderer upgrades are in scope, independent of a plan or docs edit.
additions.justification: Expresses the source's state-based MUST and its note that output changes when the plan or the renderer changes; adds no new obligation.
